Subject: Q1 usage review & renewal — capacity + term proposal

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the time on Tuesday. Attached is a brief Q1 usage summary for OptiFinance and a quick note on observed performance and spend patterns. High level: token spend is up 38% QoQ driven by two new product flows, average p99 latency is holding under 180ms for hosted routes, and the KV prefix cache is saving ~18% of token generation on repeat queries.

We’re coming up on your renewal window in late March — before we produce a formal renewal quote, wanted to align on a short health review and discuss a couple of expansion options that should reduce unit costs while meeting the higher throughput you’re seeing. Proposed agenda:
- Review Q1 token/embedding spend and per-route cost breakdown (attached)
- Performance summary and recommended config changes (batching/KV cache)
- Proposed Dedicated capacity uplift and term options (12 vs 24 months)
- ROI recap and next steps

Are you available next Wed (Feb 18) for a 30-minute review? I’ve cc’d Rishi for commercial context and Priyom for the technical bits.

Attachments: 2026_Q1_OptiFinance_usage_report.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Marissa

Claire — quick note ahead of our call. We’ll model three commercial scenarios for the meeting:
1) Renew hosted at current T&Cs (baseline)
2) 12-month Dedicated commit with modest uplift (+30% capacity) and a 15% usage discount
3) 24-month Dedicated commit with larger uplift (+60% capacity) and a 25% usage discount + reserved burst capacity

I’ll bring preliminary $/month and $/effective-1M-token numbers. If you prefer, we can also show a blended model where Settlement stays on Dedicated and lower-latency Reconciliation remains on hosted with routing policies.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Q1 usage review & renewal — capacity + term proposal

Claire — quick technical note before the review. From the telemetry:
- Settlement flow: median tokens/req = 220, 95th pct = 1.1k; this flow benefits heavily from KV prefix caching (current cache hit ~24%).
- Reconciliation flow: median tokens/req = 40, 95th pct = 280; high sensitivity to p99 latency spikes.

Recommendations:
- For Settlement: move to Dedicated vCPU/GPU pool configured with aggressive KV caching + a 64-token dynamic batch window. That will reduce token generation by ~20–25% and smooth tail latency.
- For Reconciliation: keep on hosted with an optimized batching policy (small batch sizes, higher priority routing) to preserve sub-100ms median latency for interactive users.

If you choose a hybrid approach we estimate a net cost reduction of ~22% vs current spend with a 24-month commit; 12-month commit shows ~14% savings. I’ll bring the config diff and a short perf run in the review.

Attachments referenced: perf-sim-output.csv (attached during meeting)

Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
